content:
**The five most‑populous countries in 2023 and the rivers that run through their capital cities**

| Rank (2023) | Country (population ≈ 2023) | Capital city | Major river(s) that flow through the capital* | Key source for population | Key source for river information |
|------------|----------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| 1 | **China** – ~1.41 billion | **Beijing** | **Yong Ding River** (part of the Hai River basin) – the historic “Yongding” runs across the northern suburbs of Beijing and has been the city’s main watercourse for centuries. | United Nations, *World Population Prospects 2022* (2023 revision) – https://population.un.org/wpp/ | *Encyclopaedia Britannica* – “Yongding River”, *Beijing Municipal Waterworks Bureau* – river‑network description |
| 2 | **India** – ~1.40 billion | **New Delhi** (part of the National Capital Territory of Delhi) | **Yamuna River** – the Yamuna bisects Delhi from north‑west to south‑east; New Delhi’s central government precinct lies on its left (western) bank. | United Nations, *World Population Prospects 2022* (2023 revision) | *Encyclopaedia Britannica* – “Yamuna River”; Government of Delhi – “Geography of Delhi” |
| 3 | **United States** – ~332 million | **Washington, D.C.** | **Potomac River** – forms the southern and western border of the federal district; the iconic view of the Capitol and the White House is set against the Potomac. (The **Anacostia River**, a tributary, also runs through the city’s eastern side.) | United Nations, *World Population Prospects 2022* (2023 revision) | *U.S. Geological Survey* (USGS) – “Potomac River Basin”; *Washington, D.C. Office of Planning* – “Geography & Waterways” |
| 4 | **Indonesia** – ~275 million | **Jakarta** | **Ciliwung River** – originates on the slopes of West Java and traverses central Jakarta before emptying into the Java Sea. (Other urban streams such as the **Sunter** and **Pesanggrahan** rivers also cross the metropolitan area, but Ciliwung is the historic main channel.) | United Nations, *World Population Prospects 2022* (2023 revision) | *Encyclopaedia Britannica* – “Ciliwung River”; Jakarta Water Authority – “River Management in Jakarta” |
| 5 | **Pakistan** – ~240 million | **Islamabad** | **Soan River** (and its tributary the **Khanpur/Islamabad Stream**) – the Soan runs just west of the city, separating Islamabad from its twin city Rawalpindi; the small Khanpur stream cuts through the southern part of Islamabad and feeds the Rawal Lake reservoir. | United Nations, *World Population Prospects 2022* (2023 revision) | *Encyclopaedia Britannica* – “Soan River”; Capital Development Authority (CDA) – “Geography of Islamabad” |

\* Where a capital is traversed by more than one watercourse, the river listed is the **principal/most‑recognised** one—i.e., the one that most maps, official documents and local descriptions cite as the city’s defining river.

---

### Quick reference summary

- **Beijing, China** – **Yong Ding River** (Hai River system)  
- **New Delhi, India** – **Yamuna River**  
- **Washington, D.C., USA** – **Potomac River** (plus Anacostia tributary)  
- **Jakarta, Indonesia** – **Ciliwung River**  
- **Islamabad, Pakistan** – **Soan River** (with the smaller Khanpur/Islamabad stream)

These rivers have shaped each capital’s history, layout, and water‑resource management, and they continue to be central to urban planning, flood control, and cultural identity.
